original_question: Which spectral types can occur for ergodic measure-preserving automorphisms? In particular, does there exist an ergodic automorphism with absolutely continuous spectrum that is not Lebesgue, and which sets of spectral multiplicities can be realized by ergodic automorphisms?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Q3: "What spectra can ergodic automorphisms have? Does there exist an automorphism with absolutely continuous non-Lebesgue spectrum? What sets of spectral multiplicities can an ergodic automorphism have?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's Q3 almost verbatim: it asks which spectra can occur for ergodic automorphisms, whether absolutely continuous but non-Lebesgue spectrum can occur, and which spectral multiplicity sets are realizable.
missing_details: The paper is working with ergodic automorphisms of a probability space, not arbitrary measure-preserving transformations in general or the separate σ-finite setting.

To make the question fully stand-alone, one should specify that the spectrum is the Koopman spectrum of the associated unitary operator, usually considered on the orthocomplement of the constants L^2_0(X,μ) in the probability-space case.

The phrase "absolutely continuous but not Lebesgue" should be made precise as a statement about maximal spectral type: absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on the unit circle, but not equivalent to Lebesgue measure.
The phrase "sets of spectral multiplicities" should be defined as the essential values of the spectral multiplicity function in the spectral decomposition.

The paper places next to Q3 a different nearby problem, Q4, asking about finite-multiplicity absolutely continuous spectrum (the weakened Banach problem); your draft does not explicitly separate Q3 from that adjacent question.
refined_question: For an ergodic measure-preserving automorphism T of a probability space (X,μ), viewed through its Koopman operator U_T on L^2_0(X,μ), what spectra can occur? More specifically, can U_T have maximal spectral type that is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on the unit circle but not equivalent to Lebesgue measure, and which sets can occur as the spectral multiplicity set of U_T?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Section 1, Q3. The immediately preceding Banach-problem discussion supplies the probability-space convention and explains that, in the probability setting, one works on the subspace orthogonal to the constants. The immediately following Q4 is a separate neighboring question about finite-multiplicity absolutely continuous spectrum, and Theorem 1.1 uses that Q4 in a different dichotomy involving positive local rank and multiple mixing. So the paper-faithful target is Q3, sharpened only by making the Koopman-operator and maximal-spectral-type language explicit.
